record.paper_title: Vector bundles on curves and generalized theta functions: recent results and open problems
record.context_brief: Analytic realization of generalized theta functions
record.original_question: Let X be a compact Riemann surface of genus g ≥ 2, let SU_X(r) be the moduli space of semistable rank-r vector bundles on X with trivial determinant, and let L be the determinant line bundle. Is there a sufficiently simple and flexible way to express elements of H^0(SU_X(r), L^k), viewed as non-abelian generalized theta functions, as holomorphic functions?

evidence.quote: There is however one aspect of the picture which is missing so far in higher rank, namely the analytic description of the sections of O(kΘ) as holomorphic functions.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a compact Riemann surface of genus $g \geq 2$. Let $\mathcal{SU}_X(r)$ denote the moduli space of semistable rank-$r$ holomorphic vector bundles on $X$ with trivial determinant, and let $\mathcal{L}$ be the determinant line bundle on $\mathcal{SU}_X(r)$ (the ample generator of $\mathrm{Pic}(\mathcal{SU}_X(r)) \cong \mathbb{Z}$). For an integer $k \geq 1$, the global sections $H^0(\mathcal{SU}_X(r), \mathcal{L}^k)$ are called non-abelian (generalized) theta functions of rank $r$ and level $k$. In the abelian case $r=1$, such sections admit a classical description as explicit holomorphic theta series in coordinates on the Jacobian.

Provide a sufficiently simple and flexible analytic description that realizes the elements of $H^0(\mathcal{SU}_X(r), \mathcal{L}^k)$ as concrete holomorphic functions (in suitable coordinates or on a suitable covering/parameter space), generalizing the classical theta-series description available for $r=1$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of giving an explicit, flexible analytic realization of non-abelian theta functions as holomorphic functions appears to remain open. While there are connections to conformal blocks (Verlinde formula), addition formulae, and partial results in low rank/genus or via Szegő kernels, no fully satisfactory explicit holomorphic-function description analogous to the classical $r=1$ theta series is known in higher rank.

status_evidence.title: Theta Functions, Old and New (Beauville)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discussing generalized theta functions and identifying explicit analytic description in higher rank as a missing aspect.
status_evidence.claim: Explicit holomorphic-function realization of non-abelian theta functions in higher rank is identified as an outstanding question.

status_evidence.title: Addition formulae for non-Abelian theta functions and applications
status_evidence.snippet: Generalizes formulae from Jacobian theta functions to non-abelian theta functions, including links to the Szegő kernel.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results extend classical theta-function formulae to the non-abelian setting but do not provide a complete explicit description.

status_evidence.title: Quantum mechanics and non-abelian theta functions for SU(2)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies non-abelian theta functions in the SU(2) case via quantum-mechanical/conformal block methods.
status_evidence.claim: Explicit constructions exist in special cases (e.g., rank 2) but a uniform simple analytic description remains elusive.
